title: WHEN CRITICISM HIDES A DEEPER MOTIVE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Miriam and Aaron began to talk against Moses because of his Cushite wife, for he had married a Cushite. "Has the Lord spoken only through Moses?" they asked. "Hasn't he also spoken through us?" And the Lord heard this. — Num 12:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Miriam and Aaron start by criticising Moses' wife, but their real complaint slips out in the very next breath: "Hasn't the Lord also spoken through us?" The marriage was just the cover story. Underneath was jealousy — resentment that Moses held a place they wanted for themselves.

How often our complaints work the same way. We raise one objection out loud while a very different feeling stirs quietly beneath. We criticise a decision when we are really nursing hurt pride. We find fault with a person when we are actually envious of their standing. The stated reason and the true reason are not always the same.

The most sobering line here is short and quiet: "And the Lord heard this." They may have thought it was a private family conversation between siblings. But nothing spoken against another is ever truly hidden from God. He hears not only our words but the motives curled up inside them.

This calls us to honesty. Before we voice a criticism, it is worth asking God to show us what is really driving it. Is this genuine concern, or wounded pride wearing a mask? The Lord who hears everything also offers to cleanse the heart. Bring your true motives to Him, and let Him deal with them before they do damage.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When you criticise others, what is often the real motive underneath?
2. How does knowing "the Lord heard this" change how you speak about people?
3. Is there jealousy in your heart that you have been disguising as concern?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You hear not only my words but the motives behind them. Search my heart and expose the jealousy and pride I try to hide. Cleanse me and make my words honest and kind. Amen.
